title: Deterministic quant checkpoint indexing & artifact identity ledger
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Calibration runs for FP8/INT8 produce many artifacts (calibration tables, quant profiles, validation goldens, config manifests). Currently artifacts are named by timestamp or developer-chosen labels which makes reproducibility, automated rollback, and compact lookup difficult. Goal: provide a deterministic indexing and compact identity ledger for quant checkpoints so any artifact can be reconstructed, verified, and rolled back by automated pipelines and runtime agents. Scope: - deterministic artifact identity scheme (content-hash + stable metadata fingerprint) - signed manifest format that binds model commit, dataset snapshot, seed/config, toolchain version, and quant profile - an append-only compact ledger (index) for fast lookup by model-version, profile-name, or accuracy-slug - CLI + service APIs to register, query, and mark rollback states - integration with release/canary flow and runtime fallback selection (compatible variant mapping) Out of scope: complete UI in Console (will follow after core API + backend), long-term archival policy (handled by infra team).
acceptance_criteria: All calibration artifacts (calibration table, quant profile, validation metrics, calibration config) produced by our canonical calibrator are registered with a deterministic identifier (sha256 over canonicalized payload) and a stable metadata fingerprint
Every registered artifact has a signed manifest that includes model_commit, dataset_snapshot_id, calibrator_version, random_seed, input_shapes_distribution_hash, and validation_golden_id
Rollback API can mark a model deployment to use a prior artifact identifier and the runtime can fetch a compatible binary variant automatically
A compact ledger (query service) supports queries by model_commit, profile_name, and accuracy_delta threshold and returns canonical artifact identifiers within 100ms p95
Migration script exists to index the last 18 months of calibration outputs into the ledger with integrity verification and a migration audit report
technical_notes: Identifier design: content-addressable id = sha256(CANONICAL_JSON(payload)) using stable key ordering and UTF-8 normalized strings; separate fingerprint = blake2b-128(metadata-json) for compact indexes

Manifest format: flat JSON with fields: artifact_id, fingerprint, signed_by, signature, model_commit, dataset_snapshot, calibrator_semver, seed, training_config_hash, input_shape_histogram_hash, validation_goldens (list of ids), created_at
Signing: use internal KMS-managed keypair to sign manifests; signatures attached as base64; rotation handled via key-version metadata so older manifests remain verifiable

Ledger storage: append-only immutable index table in CockroachDB with bloom-filtered secondary lookup tables for model_commit and profile_name; store pointers to object store (S3) for full artifact blobs

Reconstruction: provide a deterministic CLI (redwood-quantctl) with a `reconstruct --artifact-id` command that pulls blobs, verifies checksums, replays calibration with captured seed and config, and produces a byte-for-byte match of calibration table

Compatibility mapping: maintain compatibility rules mapping quant profile variants (e.g., fp8-e4m3 -> quantized-runtime-compatible-binary) so runtime can automatically fallback to nearest compatible artifact if exact artifact not available
Integrity: implement periodic ledger rehash job that recomputes fingerprints for a sample of entries and raises alerts on mismatch; sample rate 1% daily and 100% for any migration run
Performance: index queries optimized for 100ms p95 via precomputed materialized views for hot model commits and a small in-memory LRU cache in query API
rollout_steps: Build schema and service + CLI for artifact registration + verification (unit + integration tests)
Run migration in staging against snapshot of production calibration outputs and validate via migration audit report
Canary: enable registration and lookup for 5% of new calibration runs and use ledger-driven lookup in non-critical test clusters
Full: flip registrars to register all new artifacts; enable runtime to respect ledger lookups for deploys with automatic fallback configured
Monitor: set SLOs for registration latency, query latency, and reconstruction time; track mismatches and rollback events
Postmortem: 2-week stabilization window, then PRD update for Console integration
